label: absolute position >= 5 before copying (late original tokens and <DEL>)
explanation: Position counter. Fires on every input step at absolute position t >= 5 during the original phase, and on the <DEL> step whenever L >= 5, regardless of token identity (in_tok, prev_tok, first_tok, next_out all flat). Magnitude ramps with absolute step t, roughly 0.3 of max at t=5, 0.55 at t=6, 0.78 at t=7, 0.95 at t=8, and the <DEL> at t=9 reaches the max. The <DEL> step follows the same ramp: about 0.25 for L=5, 0.5 for L=6, 0.7 for L=7. Never fires at t <= 3, never on short sequences (L=3,4), and never during the copy phase. The only misses are near-zero activations (<=0.02 of max, 0.1% of mass) at t=4 on some sequences with L >= 5.

issues: The core claims hold up. On test the predicate (t >= 5) & (phase <= 1) scores precision 1.0 (0 false positives), recall 0.932, F1 0.965 and mass recall 0.999. The profile confirms it never fires at t <= 3, on L = 3 or 4, or in the copy phase (0 of 2.73M steps). It fires on 100% of original steps with orig_idx >= 5 and on every <DEL> with L >= 5 (414480 of 500000). Rates are flat across in_tok, prev_tok, prev2_tok, next_out and first_tok.

The only misses are at t = 4 (18% of all t = 4 steps, all with L >= 5). Their activations are at most 0.01 of max, so they are a small systematic but near-zero class holding 0.1% of the mass. Adding t = 4 & L >= 5 to the predicate lowers precision to 0.80 and F1 to 0.89, so the original predicate is the better one.

One numeric claim is wrong. The explanation says the <DEL> magnitude is about 0.25 for L=5, 0.5 for L=6 and 0.7 for L=7. The test examples show about 0.51 for L=5, 0.69-0.72 for L=6 and 0.76-0.87 for L=7. <DEL> sits about one step higher than an original token at the same t (t=5 token about 0.29, t=5 <DEL> about 0.51). This is a minor magnitude error and does not affect the label or predicate.
